tests.opsz: matched to CSS size at both raster scales

ui.reason: Core RU/EN UI samples are readable at 12–18 px at 400/500 in this rasterizer. Thin 100 is too pale for routine small UI; 900 has dense small counters and should be reserved for emphasis.

headings.reason: 18 px heading-sized labels at 400/500/900 survive. Larger display sizes were outside this review; Thin needs contrast and size appropriate to its intended role.

body.reason: Short RU/EN body strings at 14–18 px 400/500 show no visible broken strokes, mark collisions, or filled counters. 12 px is less comfortable and 100/900 are not recommended body defaults.

sustained_reading.reason: Short raster strings cannot establish sustained reading performance, comfort, line-length effects, or fatigue.

findings.title: Thin loses practical contrast at small 1x sizes
findings.concrete_evidence: proof-12-100-1x.png and proof-14-100-1x.png: EN/RU stems and dots are markedly pale relative to 400; contours remain recognizable. The 2x 12 px render gives more stable edges. This is an expected Thin limitation, not evidence of malformed outlines.
findings.recommendation: Use 400/500 for routine 12–14 px UI and body; document Thin as display/emphasis rather than small reading text.
findings.acceptance_test: Compare the same strings at native 1x/2x in target OS/browser engines and confirm normal UI defaults use 400 or higher.

findings.title: Supplementary accented Latin probes lack coverage
findings.concrete_evidence: Final probe line ends in three identical oval missing-glyph forms for é ï Å at every weight. getBestCmap confirms all three absent; ё and й are mapped. This is a coverage failure, not raster mark positioning.
findings.recommendation: If accented Latin names or international text are promised, add these glyphs and decomposition/mark support; otherwise explicitly limit repertoire.
findings.acceptance_test: HarfBuzz shaping of é ï Å must return nonzero intended glyphs and visual accents at 12–18 px in supported engines.

positive_evidence: 400/500 core RU/EN strokes survive; counters remain identifiable in sampled native crops.
At 900 12 px counters in а/е/в/8 are small, but no definite fully closed counter was established.
Russian ё dots and й breve remain above their bases and do not visibly collide in tested lines.
limits: FreeType grayscale + HarfBuzz via existing scripts/render.py; not actual hardware, CoreText, DirectWrite, or browser screenshots.
1x renders at CSS ppem; 2x renders at twice ppem with identical CSS opsz. 2x images are backing-store pixel proofs, not a measured Retina viewing study.
Large overview images were resized by image viewer; pixel-level judgments relied on 14 individual crops.
Short black-on-white strings only; no dark mode, LCD subpixel rendering, low contrast, fractional CSS sizing, multiline clipping, or sustained reading study.
Accented Latin probes are supplementary to basic RU/EN scope.
No previous or current report/review consulted; font/source unchanged.
